approaches.name: SIRAGE EMIS for school mapping, identifiers and refugee statistics
approaches.description: Uses the SIRAGE education management information system to map schools, assign linked unique identifiers, and track refugee enrollment for planning. Practices: SIRAGE EMIS data used for school mapping (Carte Scolaire) and infrastructure/teacher deployment planning; Operationalization of SIRAGE for real-time collection, reporting and analysis of enrollment, teacher, infrastructure and learning data; SIRAGE unique identifiers linked to national ID and Khidmety; SIRAGE refugee module for education statistics; climate vulnerability indicators in school mapping data systems; SIRAGE refugee module tracking refugee children enrollment.
approaches.why_innovative: Digital core: SIRAGE EMIS | New: EMIS data reused to revive school mapping for school completion and teacher deployment | Adoption: Program will leverage SIRAGE data | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: SIRAGE presents a valuable opportunity to address this issue, particularly by leveraging its data to revive school mapping (Carte Scolaire) and ensuring that infrastructure investments prioritize the completion of existing schools and the efficient deployment of teachers.

extra_evidence.text: The Education Management Information System (EMIS, Système d'Information de Gestion de l'Éducation, renamed SIRAGE), deployed through the World Bankfinanced Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143), is an important tool for managing the education system and informing data-driven decision-making.
The operationalization of SIRAGE32 will enable real-time data collection, reporting, and analysis.

By covering areas such as student enrollment, teacher deployment, school infrastructure, and learning outcomes, SIRAGE will provide actionable insights to education policy makers and ensure that resources and interventions are tailored to local needs.
SIRAGE is now used as the main administrative tool for the education sector, assigning unique identifiers to teachers and children, linking them to parents’ national identification numbers.
SIRAGE is fully integrated with the digitized national public services platform ‘Khidmety’.
Year 1 milestone requires full deployment of SIRAGE refugee module.
Strengthened data systems will incorporate climate vulnerability indicators to inform school mapping, infrastructure planning, and rapid response to disruptions.
An additional US$600,000 will be disbursed upon the full deployment of the refugee module under SIRAGE.

Full deployment is defined as: the module is live in SIRAGE production environment, populated with data from at least the most recent complete school year, accessible to authorized MERSE users, and validated by the SIRAGE technical team.

category.rationale: Technological: EMIS dataset is the core mechanism enabling planning

sector.rationale: School mapping and deployment planning is an education system management/administration function.

approaches.name: Hybrid digital and AI teacher training platform
approaches.description: Delivers continuous teacher training and coaching through the Tenwir hybrid platform and AI, including a refugee-specific module, tracked in SIRAGE. Practices: AI and digital hybrid teaching/coaching platform (Tenwir); continuous teacher training digital platform; Hybrid distance teacher training via CFED tracked in SIRAGE/Tenwir; Refugee-specific module in hybrid distance teacher training; Hybrid online plus in-person teacher training model; Tenwir digital platform for teacher training delivery.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: AI-assisted hybrid teacher coaching platform - cue: 'artificial intelligence' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, rare_or_absent before 2019

evidence.text: The Program will leverage the use of digital technology and artificial intelligence for teaching and coaching, using 30 Targeted communities are the highest concentration areas for refugees in the country: Wilaya of Hodh El CHarqi, Wilaya of Nouakchott South, Wilaya of Nouakchott West, Wilaya of Nouakchott North and Wilaya of Dakhlet Nouadhibou.

extra_evidence.text: Page 9 Official Use Only The World Bank Mauritania Improving Education Quality, Results, and Access for All Operation (IQRAA, P509243) the hybrid approach and platform (Tenwir) developed under the Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143).
To address this, a strategic approach involves implementing a continuous training digital platform, as successfully established by the ongoing Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143).
This platform facilitates ongoing professional development for teachers, making training more accessible and engaging.

Data source/ Agency Verification Entity Procedure NPP/MASEF IVA Annual validation by IVA DLI 2: Teachers trained in the application of modern pedagogical approaches using the new hybrid model Amount to be disbursed = US$4,500,000 Baseline = 0 Target = 12,500 In Year 1, US$500,000 will be disbursed upon the development and validation by MERSE/UNHCR of the refugee-specific Formula training module and its incorporation into the official hybrid teacher training model delivered through Distance Learning and Exchange (Centre de Formation et d’Echange a Distance, CFED) and tracked in SIRAGE/Tenwir.

In Year 1, this indicator will incentivize and reward the development and rollout of refugee-specific training module integrated into the hybrid teacher training model, addressing pedagogical approaches for refugee and mixed (refugee/host community) classrooms, including multilingual and Arabic-medium instruction strategies.

It refers to teachers who have participated in distance and/or in-person (hybrid) professional development programs aimed at enhancing teacher effectiveness, especially for refugees and host communities, thereby affecting student learning outcomes.

A trained teacher is defined as having successfully completed at least three of the following training modules (numeracy, literacy [French or Arabic], pedagogy, scripted lessons method, and refugee-specific) developed under the new hybrid continuous teacher training model.

Climate Action Incorporated DLI RA1: Improve the quality of basic education (of which US$11.5 million equivalent IDA) Adaptation: DLI 2: Teachers trained in the application of modern pedagogical approaches using the new hybrid model (US$4.5 million equivalent IDA) • The shift to a hybrid (online + in-person) model is a structural adaptation of the education system: Trained teachers can maintain learning continuity remotely, including when climate events make physical attendance impossible. • Each teacher trained in the hybrid model becomes a climate-resilient asset capable of switching delivery modes during climate disruptions, creating a direct and demonstrable link between the financed activity and reduced climate vulnerability. • Teacher training on climate-responsive pedagogy, psychosocial support during climate shocks, and classroom risk preparedness. • This DLI will also have a focus on refugee and host community teachers, directly addressing climate-induced displacement, which is one of the most acute climate impacts in the Sahel region.

Mitigation: • The digital training platform (Tenwir) substitutes for long-distance travel to centralized training centers across Mauritania's vast territory, reducing travelrelated greenhouse gas emissions. • Training 12,500 teachers in digital content delivery reduces demand for printed materials at scale, generating measurable reductions in paper production and distribution emissions. • Teacher training using a hybrid delivery model is the foundational enabling activity for Mauritania's broader digital education ecosystem (virtual labs, artificial intelligence coaching, SIRAGE).

approaches.description: Makes SIRAGE the single sector management tool, with yearbook production and DLI data verified by an independent agency. Practices: SIRAGE as single sector management tool with timely yearbook production as a DLI; SIRAGE-sourced DLI data verified by an Independent Verification Agency.

evidence.text: The Basic Education Sector Support Project (P163143) has supported the establishment of a strong management system, known as SIRAGE, which the Government is committed to using as a singular management tool for Page 17 Official Use Only The World Bank Mauritania Improving Education Quality, Results, and Access for All Operation (IQRAA, P509243) the sector.

extra_evidence.text: The Program has incorporated the timely production of yearbooks as a DLI, emphasizing the importance of leveraging SIRAGE capabilities.
This strategic action aims to ensure that SIRAGE is effectively utilized and that necessary data are collected timely, thereby reinforcing the system's capacity to support informed decision-making.
To ensure impartiality, the achievement of DLIs will be verified by an Independent Verification Agency (IVA), a firm contracted by the PCU under terms satisfactory to the World Bank.
Most of the DLI data will be sourced from SIRAGE.
The PCU will consolidate the necessary information to confirm compliance with each DLI and submit it to the IVA.

evidence.text: The Program is designed to drive system-wide change, leveraging results-based financing to incentivize institutional reform and achieve sustainable educational improvements.

extra_evidence.text: A robust M&E framework will underpin Program implementation, utilizing SIRAGE for real-time data collection and monitoring.

For subsequent years (Year 2–Year 5), US$500,000 is disbursed each year when the statistical yearbook generated by SIRAGE has been produced and published on MERSE's Formula website no later than December 15 of the calendar year in which the school year to which it relates ends and used for sector planning and monitoring.

The statistical yearbook must include at least the following five key chapters for each education cycle (preprimary, primary, and secondary): (a) synthetic data and global indicators (enrollment rate, transition rate, success rate in national examinations);

Page 41 Official Use Only The World Bank Mauritania Improving Education Quality, Results, and Access for All Operation (IQRAA, P509243) In Year 1, this indicator will assess and reward the effective deployment of ECE and inclusive education/special educational needs modules in SIRAGE.

In addition, this indicator will assess and reward the effective deployment of the refugee module, a key WHR-supported institutional reform critical for tracking refugee children enrollment and Description progression in the national education system.

Data source/ Agency SIRAGE/MERSE Website/UNHCR Verification Entity IVA Year 1: The IVA will verify that the three SIRAGE modules (ECE, refugee, and inclusive education) are live in the production environment, populated with at least one full year of data, and accessible to authorized users, based on a technical review of the SIRAGE system and written confirmation from the SIRAGE technical team.
